source.title: Developments, Applications and Open Problems in Fixed Point Theory

accepted.question_text: A Banach space X has the weak fixed point property (WFPP) when every weakly compact convex subset K of X has the fixed point property: every nonexpansive self-map T: K -> K, meaning ||T x - T y|| <= ||x - y|| for all x,y in K, has at least one fixed point in K. Is it true that every Banach space has the weak fixed point property?

evidence.quote: A mapping T: K -> K is said to be nonexpansive if ||Tx - Ty|| <= ||x - y|| for all x,y in K. We define K as possessing the fixed point property (FPP) if each nonexpansive map defined on K has a fixed point within K. Moreover, we define X as having the FPP if every closed bounded convex subset of X possesses the FPP, and X has the weak FPP if each weakly compact convex subset of X has the FPP.
For quite some time, a lingering question persisted: Does every Banach space have the WFPP? In 1981, Alspach provided the initial and essentially sole known instance of a space lacking the WFPP.

accepted.question_text: Let X be a reflexive Banach space, meaning that the canonical embedding of X into its bidual X** has range equal to all of X**. Does X have the fixed point property: for every nonempty closed bounded convex subset K of X and every nonexpansive self-map T: K -> K satisfying ||T x - T y|| <= ||x - y|| for all x,y in K, must T have a fixed point in K?

evidence.quote: Definition 5.5 A normed linear space X is termed reflexive if its range R(C), where C: X -> X** is the canonical mapping, equals the second dual space X**. A reflexive normed linear space constitutes a Banach space.
A fundamental unresolved query in this realm is: Do all reflexive spaces exhibit the FPP?

accepted.question_text: A Banach space X is super-reflexive when no non-reflexive Banach space is finitely representable in X; finite representability here means that there is a number lambda > 1 such that every finite-dimensional subspace of the represented space embeds isomorphically into X with distortion bounded by lambda. Does every super-reflexive Banach space have the fixed point property, meaning that every nonempty closed bounded convex subset K of X has a fixed point for each nonexpansive self-map T: K -> K?

evidence.quote: A normed linear space X is considered finitely representable in another normed linear space Y if there exists a number lambda > 1 such that for each finite-dimensional subspace X_n of X, there exists an isomorphism T_n from X_n to Y satisfying lambda^-1 ||x|| <= ||T_n(x)|| <= lambda ||x|| if x in X_n. A super-reflexive Banach space is a Banach space X such that no non-reflexive Banach space can be finitely representable in X.
An intriguing unresolved question in this context is: Does every super-reflexive Banach space possess the FPP?

accepted.question_text: For each real p with 1 < p < infinity, take the classical sequence space ell^p and replace its norm by any equivalent norm. Does every such equivalent renorming of ell^p have the fixed point property, meaning that every nonempty closed bounded convex subset K has a fixed point for each nonexpansive self-map T: K -> K? In particular, does this hold for every equivalent renorming of ell^2?

evidence.quote: Another unresolved matter is: Does every equivalent renorming of l^p, where 1 < p < infinity, exhibit the FPP? This question remains unanswered even for l^2.

accepted.question_text: Let K be a weakly compact convex subset of a Banach space. Does K necessarily have the fixed point property for strictly contractive self-maps, meaning that every mapping T: K -> K satisfying ||T x - T y|| < ||x - y|| for all distinct x,y in K must have a fixed point in K?

evidence.quote: Two more open problems suggested by Kirk: Kirk says 'There are many open problems in metric fixed point theory, but two have frustrated me over the years because of their simplicity and yet seeming intractability'. Problem 1: Does a weakly compact convex subset K of a Banach space have the fixed point property for strictly contractive mappings (that is, mappings T: K -> K for which ||Tx - Ty|| < ||x - y||, x,y in K, x != y)?

accepted.question_text: Let K be a bounded closed convex subset of a Banach space, and let T,G: K -> K be commuting nonexpansive mappings. For epsilon > 0, define the epsilon-approximate fixed point set of a map S by F_epsilon(S) = {x in K : ||x - Sx|| <= epsilon}. Must F_epsilon(T) intersect F_epsilon(G) nontrivially for every epsilon > 0?

evidence.quote: Another problem concerns approximate fixed point sequences. It's well-established that if K is a bounded convex subset of any Banach space (or normed space), and T: K -> K is nonexpansive, then there exists a sequence {x_n} in K such that ||x_n - T(x_n)|| tends to 0 as n approaches infinity. Consequently, for each epsilon > 0, F_epsilon(T) := {x in K : ||x - Tx|| <= epsilon} != empty.

Problem 2: If K is a bounded (closed) convex subset of a Banach space and if T,G: K -> K are commuting nonexpansive mappings, is it the case that for each epsilon > 0, F_epsilon(T) cap F_epsilon(G) != empty?

trace.notes: Normalized the single ARGUMENTS value as the zbMATH resolver URL https://zbmath.org/8149276 with trailing identifier 8149276.

Direct shell fetch of the zbMATH landing page returned HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare challenge. Local project resolver data in outputs/open-problems-0418-all.csv identified the exact work as 'Developments, applications and open problems in fixed point theory' with DOI 10.1201/9781003530602-1.

Bounded exact-work recovery used exact-title, DOI, and exact-title-plus-PDF searches. The accepted readable source is the author-uploaded ResearchGate full-text page, whose visible title, DOI, book context, and pages 1-14 match the zbMATH/DOI record. A PagePlace publisher preview for the same book was also found, but local shell download failed due DNS restrictions.

Mapped the ResearchGate full-text HTML/PDF rendering. The source structure is Chapter 1 with sections 1.1 Introduction, 1.2 Extensions of the Contraction Principle, 1.3 Fixed Point Without Continuity, 1.4 Applications, and 1.5 Open Problems in Metric Fixed Point Theory. Section 1.5 is the only explicit open-problem region; it defines nonexpansive maps, FPP, WFPP, reflexivity, finite representability, and super-reflexivity before listing the candidate questions.

Extracted six explicit question candidates from Section 1.5: the historical WFPP question for all Banach spaces, FPP for all reflexive spaces, FPP for all super-reflexive spaces, FPP for every equivalent renorming of ell^p, Kirk's strict-contraction problem, and Kirk's common approximate fixed point problem for commuting nonexpansive mappings.
Expanded WFPP using the source definitions of nonexpansive map, FPP, and weak FPP. Marked solved because the same source states Alspach supplied a space lacking the WFPP.
Expanded the reflexive-space FPP question using the source definition of reflexivity and the earlier FPP definition.
Expanded the super-reflexive-space FPP question using the source definition of finite representability and super-reflexivity.
Expanded the renorming question to state the quantified range 1 < p < infinity and include the FPP target explicitly.
Kept Kirk's strict-contraction problem and inlined the strict contractive inequality from the source's parenthetical definition.
Expanded Kirk's commuting-nonexpansive-map question by defining F_epsilon(S) from the source's approximate fixed point notation.
No near-duplicates were merged. The six candidates concern distinct fixed point property settings or distinct mapping classes.

Accepted all six candidates. Each question_text is self-contained, avoids source-pointing language, has locator-backed evidence from the full-text source, and introduces only definitions supported by Section 1.5 evidence. q_001 is marked solved because the source explicitly supplies a counterexample; all others remain unsolved in the source.
